memories.content: Do not exceed two primary HCI contributions.
Name each design or empirical contribution and present it in a single sentence.
In studies recruiting community participants, emphasize the time burden associated with participation.
In studies recruiting community participants, emphasize the travel burden associated with participation.
HCI reviewers find it difficult to identify primary contributions when named design or empirical contributions exceed two.
Emphasize the core design decisions that formative evaluation will change rather than a polished product demonstration.
Emphasize design principles transferable to other similar interactions as the primary contribution, rather than the performance of a specific prototype.
Formative evaluation creates grounds for modification in subsequent iterations rather than definitively determining the superiority of design alternatives.
Mark unverified schedule assumptions as such.
Mark unverified recruitment assumptions as such.
Mark unverified technical assumptions as such.
Trace back the resources required for each core prototype feature and field research procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility by examining the personnel required for each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility by examining the equipment required for each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility by examining the time required for each procedure.
Document separately the commitments and confirmation status of field partners required for recruitment, installation, and operational support.
Designate a responsible party for software updates, equipment inspections, and user support during the deployment period.
The user's deployment readiness can be assessed only when dependencies on external services and field personnel are visible.
Field schedules and assigned personnel may change due to operational factors beyond the researcher’s control.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate review layers: one shapes HCI contribution framing, participant burden, and formative evaluation claims; the other documents operational assumptions, resources, partners, ownership, dependencies, and volatility. No shared operational claim or scope-aligned contradiction is supplied.

relations.reason: These memories state and justify one reference-only limit on the number of named primary contributions.
relations.summary: Primary HCI contributions should be limited to two so reviewers can identify them clearly.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only presentation requirement with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Each design or empirical contribution should be named and expressed in one sentence.

relations.reason: The memories split one reference-only policy across two participant-burden dimensions.
relations.summary: Community-participant studies should emphasize both the time and travel burdens of participation.

relations.reason: The memories jointly describe the reference-only purpose and evidentiary limits of formative evaluation.
relations.summary: Formative evaluation should foreground design decisions open to iteration rather than polished demonstration or definitive superiority claims.

relations.reason: This reference-only contribution-framing claim is independent of the formative-evaluation and contribution-count policies.
relations.summary: Transferable design principles should be presented as the primary contribution instead of a particular prototype's performance.

relations.reason: The memories split one compared-only assumption-labeling policy across three assumption types.
relations.summary: Unverified schedule, recruitment, and technical assumptions should be explicitly labeled.

relations.reason: This compared-only traceability requirement covers both prototype features and research procedures and has no reference counterpart.
relations.summary: Required resources should be traced for every core prototype feature and field-research procedure.

relations.reason: The memories split one compared-only feasibility criterion across three resource categories.
relations.summary: Operational feasibility review should examine the personnel, equipment, and time required for each procedure.

relations.reason: This is a compared-only requirement for recording partner commitments across deployment functions.
relations.summary: Field-partner commitments and confirmation status should be documented separately for recruitment, installation, and operational support.

relations.reason: This compared-only ownership requirement is independently useful and has no reference counterpart.
relations.summary: A responsible party should be designated for updates, inspections, and user support throughout deployment.

relations.reason: This compared-only readiness condition concerns dependency visibility rather than partner confirmation or task ownership.
relations.summary: Deployment readiness assessment requires visible dependencies on external services and field personnel.

relations.reason: This compared-only risk statement identifies operational volatility independently of the policies for labeling assumptions or documenting commitments.
relations.summary: Operational factors outside researcher control may change field schedules and assigned personnel.

reports.compared_only: Compared uniquely addresses assumption labeling, resource-based feasibility, partner commitments, deployment ownership and dependencies, and operational changes to schedules and staffing.
reports.reference_only: Reference uniquely limits and formats HCI contributions, foregrounds participant time and travel burdens, and frames formative work around transferable principles and iterative design modification.
